§6Pneumatic Tubes§f

§aItems teleport through pipes using compressed air. Faster than belts, but costs more to set up.§f

Pneumatic Tubes send items instantly through a network, unlike slow-moving conveyors. They need §bcompressed air§f (minimum 1 PU) and consume §e50mB§f per operation (200mB/s when busy).

Range scales with pressure: §b1 PU§f = 10m, §b2 PU§f = 25m, §b3 PU§f = 100m, §b4 PU§f = 250m, §b5 PU§f = 1000m. The range is direct distance, not line length, so a 500m loop with endpoints next to each other works on 1 PU.

Ejecting tubes have §e15§f filter slots with whitelist/blacklist, configurable recipient order (round robin, sorted, random), and source order (first, last, random slot).

§ePS:§f Use tubes for long-distance transport and belts for local sorting. Combine both for optimal factory logistics.
